REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 25, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
AUGUST 25, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by City Clerk Vida Barone.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Campers-in-Leadership members Isabella
  Gonzalez and Tosin Agbelemose.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  The following Proclamations were presented:

  La Palma-Cerritos American Association of University Women (AAUW) – (Women’s
  Equality Day).

  Pioneer Medical Group (Business Spotlight)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Ray Sell expressed concerns with the traffic surrounding the Towne Center.

  Gail Grossman spoke regarding the Cerritos Air Disaster and the pride she has in
  the diverse Cerritos community.

  Neil Estrada, Filipino-American Chamber of Commerce of Orange County, presented
  an award to the City.
 City of Cerritos  August 25, 2016

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 25, 2016
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 25, 2016 in the total amount of
  $5,694,224.39 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated August 25, 2016 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency dated
  August 25, 2016 in the amount of $4,111.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).The motion
  carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August
  11, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 11, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Adopt Ordinance No. 1006, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING
  CHAPTER 20.30 AND CHAPTER 22.40 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO THE REGULATION OF BOARDING HOUSES WITHIN THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2016-4
  (COUNCIL).*
  *Waiver of full reading approved at introduction of ordinance on August 11, 2016.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to adopt Ordinance

  CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT
  2016-4 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  (continued)

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of Bid No. 1251-17, Water quality analyses and laboratory services
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to award Bid No. 1251-
  17 to Enthalphy Analytical for the provision of Water Quality Analyses and
  Laboratory Services for a term of one (1) year with an option to renew on an annual
  basis for up to three (3) additional years (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as
  follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7F.  Approval of a change order to the contract with Psomas Engineering for design
  services for Valley View Utility relocation, Project No. 17105 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve a change
  order in an amount not to exceed $17,819 as an addition to the contract with
  Psomas Engineering under Project No. 17105 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0)
  as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of consent to the assignment of a sublease and approval of
  an estoppel and consent in connection with the assignment of the leasehold interest
  in the Vintage Cerritos Senior Housing Congregate Care Facility located at 11000
  New Falcon Way, Cerritos, California, 90703, from Avalon at Cerritos LLC, a
  California Limited Liability Company, to Welltower Inc., A Delaware Corporation, or
  its affiliate (7016-007-001,7016-007-002) (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.
 City of Cerritos  August 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to authorize the City
  Manager/Executive Director, or his designee, to execute the document(s) to facilitate,
  acknowledge and consent to the transfer of the sublease (APN 7016-007-001, 7016-
  007-002) from Avalon at Cerritos, LLC, a California limited liability company, to
  Welltower Inc., a Delaware corporation, or another affiliate approved by the City, in
  such form as the City Manager shall deem appropriate, including any estoppel
  certificates, assignment consent, or related implementing documentation required to
  appropriate in connection with completion of such assignment (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration of potential budget expenditure reduction measures
  (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, Public Hearing items 8B and 8C were
  considered concurrently.

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Budget Manager.  A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  City Clerk Vida Barone announced that written comments for the record were
  submitted by Marlene Rofe, Jim McMahon, and Mayor George Ray. These items are
  public record and available in the City Clerk’s Office.

  Ralph Westfall spoke regarding balancing the City’s budget, not raising taxes, and
  expenses related to the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Gail Grossman submitted a petition for the record requesting the budget to be
  balanced without raising taxes or dipping into reserve funds.

  Ram Kakkar spoke about profiling, benefits given to the previous and existing City
  Councils, and costs to run the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Josh Nass expressed concerns regarding administrative costs, employee to resident
  ratio, costs to run the CCPA, the Sheriff’s contract, and the Library.

  Mike Abell stated he would like “management by the numbers,” and requested
  additional charts and budget information about the Sheriff’s contract and the Library.

  Harold Cohen expressed support to keep the existing Sheriff’s station and inquired if
  the contract can be merged with the City of Artesia for service to both cities. He also
  spoke about the performances at the CCPA.
 City of Cerritos  August 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  Dan E. Nino expressed concerns with raising sales tax in the City and requested more
  public hearings on the matter. He also spoke about merging commissions and
  committees and to consider stopping of subsidies to community organizations.

  William Mayfield expressed concerns regarding the Sheriff’s contract and perquisites
  given to Sheriff’s staff.

  Jay Gray expressed concerns regarding health benefits for City Councilmembers. He
  also spoke regarding other cuts the City can make including travel, community events,
  the CPPA, participation in the utility business, the Astor museum, and renegotiation of
  the Sheriff’s contract.

  Marty Grossman requested additional public hearings and announcements before the
  consideration of budget cuts, consolidated elections, and consideration of the Sheriff’s
  contract. He also expressed concerns with the costs of the CCPA and Astor museum,
  commissioners, subsidies to community organizations, and retirement of the City
  Manager.

  Anantha Ramachandran expressed concern there were no proposed cuts to payroll,
  costs related to property acquisition and the Astor museum, and expansion of Heritage
  Park. He also spoke in opposition to the proposed sales tax measure.

  Carol Horn expressed concerns with lack of fiscal responsibility, the need for tree
  trimming, the Astor museum, and spoke in opposition to the proposed sales tax
  measure. She requested more opportunities for public input on the proposed budget
  reductions.

  Venk Farateswaran expressed concerns with going back to an area Sheriff station and
  suggested cutting pay, pension or medical benefits for retirees.

  Daniel Brewer spoke in opposition to any proposed closure of the Sheriff’s station. He
  expressed concerns with Councilmember benefits, costs of auto museum and CCPA,
  and the lack of tree trimming and sidewalk repair in the City.

  Matt Johnson expressed concerns with the position the State had put the City in, and
  while is he not in favor of raising taxes, he understands that to continue the service
  level expected by residents, the City may have to ask the residents to vote on such a
  measure.

  Mark Bollman spoke of the benefits that Cerritos residents enjoy and suggested a
  forum to engage community stakeholders to assist in achieving a balanced budget.

  Kiyong Ma expressed support for a City police force rather than continuing with the
  Sheriff’s contract.

  Gavin Riley spoke regarding the vital services that the City should concentrate on
  providing and the need to generate more revenue through the proposed sales tax
  measure and have the residents decide based upon the services they expect to receive.
 City of Cerritos  August 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  Sherman Kappe expressed support to keep the Sheriff’s station as is and that closure
  should not be a consideration in balancing the budget. He stated that the citizens
  would be deciding whether to increase the sales tax.

  Eugene Japor expressed support for the City-sponsored community events, senior
  services, the existing Sheriff’s station, and the other quality-of-life programs the City
  provides.

  Brad Beach spoke about the high level of services that the residents receive. He
  believed that most residents were against the closure of the Sheriff’s station. He
  suggested additional meetings to elicit public input on proposed budget reductions.

  Clarence Stephens spoke in support of the high quality of life services received by
  Cerritos residents. He supports the proposed sales tax measure.

  Tobi Balma expressed concerns regarding City Councilmember benefits, the proposed
  reduction in Library hours, the auto museum, and lack of publicity for the budget
  reduction agenda items.

  Gail Grossman spoke in opposition to the proposed sales tax measure and noted that
  many residents are living on fixed incomes. She also expressed concerns with the lack
  of tree trimming and sidewalk repairs.

  Marty Grossman spoke in opposition to the proposed sales tax measure and requested
  that the City show that it can be fiscally responsible before putting the matter on the
  ballot.

  Harold Cohen spoke about the choices residents had to make during the economic
  crash that occurred eight years ago and that revenues are again on the rise. He
  suggested keeping an eye on the economy for the next few years before making any
  drastic reductions.

  Anantha Ramachandran stated that the City has a good reserve base and suggested
  using the reserves for the next several years until projected revenue increased can be
  accurately analyzed. He does not support the proposed sales tax ballot measure at this
  time.

  Jay Gray suggested further public input before the City Council places a sales tax
  increase on the ballot.

  Clarence Stephens clarified that the City Council would only be voting on placing the
  proposed sales tax increase on the ballot and that voters would have to make the
  ultimate decision.

  Tina Cho inquired whether the City could invest reserve funds in municipal bonds to
  generate more revenue.

  Harold Cohen inquired whether the proposed sales tax ballot measure would give
  options for voting for different percentages of sales tax increase.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.
 City of Cerritos  August 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to continue the public
  hearings on Items 8B and 8C to a date certain, September 22, 2016 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8C.  Review and consideration of a proposal for the development of a ballot measure
  that would place before the Cerritos electorate at the March, 2017 General
  Municipal Election the question of whether to approve a local sales tax increase
  (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, Public Hearing items 8B and 8C were
  considered concurrently. See item 8B for public comments and other detail.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to continue the public
  hearings on Items 8B and 8C to a date certain, September 22, 2016 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

  None.

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Pulido, and Chen, Mayor
  Pro Tem/Vice Chair Solanki, and Mayor/Chair Ray.

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to provide opportunities for the public to
  provide input on the relative value of each of the proposed budget cuts, possibly
  through a survey on the website, as well as other comparison metrics.

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to bring budget information, including OpenGov,
  to a more prominent place on the City’s website.
 City of Cerritos  August 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 8 of 8

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 11:13 p.m.

  s/ Vida Barone_____________________
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/ George Ray_________________
George Ray, Mayor/Chair
